_comment: Template for a Claude Code PROJECT MCP configuration — copy to <project>/.mcp.json
and commit it. Everyone on the project then gets the same servers.
This is the escape hatch for anything the claude.ai connector directory does not
offer: a local database, a self-hosted tool, a community server. claude.ai connectors
and these are separate mechanisms and do not see each other.
Every server below is COMMENTED OUT (prefixed `_disabled_`). Move an entry into the
real `mcpServers` object to enable it, and delete the ones you do not use.
CREDENTIALS: never inline. Use ${VAR} — Claude Code expands it from the environment
at launch. This file is committed; the environment is not.
Claude Code will ask for approval before using a project MCP server the first time.
That prompt is a security boundary, not an annoyance: an MCP server runs with your
privileges and its tool descriptions enter the model's context. Only enable servers

_disabled_postgres._why: Read-only Postgres access. Lets an audit check the real schema — missing indexes, missing constraints, schema drift from the ORM models — instead of inferring it from code.
_disabled_postgres._setup: Create a role with SELECT only. Never point this at a production database holding personal or clinical data.

_disabled_filesystem._why: Scoped filesystem access outside the project directory — a shared datasets folder, for example.
_disabled_filesystem._setup: List only the directories that are genuinely needed. Each one is standing access.

_disabled_playwright._why: Browser automation for driving a web UI during Phase 3 of an audit — the four states, hostile inputs, accessibility checks.
_disabled_playwright._setup: Chromium is preinstalled in Claude Code web sessions; locally, run `npx playwright install chromium` once.

_disabled_sqlite._why: Local SQLite files — common in analysis and prototype work.

_disabled_example_http_server._why: Shape of a remote MCP server reached over HTTP, with a token from the environment.
